lead.headline: Hurricane Lowell lashes Kauai with 84 mph gusts on its overnight pass
lead.dek: The Category 2 storm passed near Niihau early Tuesday with 110 mph winds; Kuhio Highway is closed at Hanalei and schools are shut on Kauai and Oahu
body: Hurricane Lowell passed near or just west of Niihau overnight as a Category 2 storm, the Central Pacific Hurricane Center said in its 11 p.m. HST advisory, which put the center about 90 miles west of Lihue with sustained winds of 110 mph, moving north-northeast at 18 mph as hurricane conditions spread across Kauai County.

The Honolulu Star-Advertiser reported gusts of 84 mph at Barking Sands and 79 mph at Lihue Airport. The Hawaii Emergency Management Agency said several thousand customers on Kauai and Oahu had lost power. Kuhio Highway stayed closed at the Hanalei Bridge, a flash flood warning for Kauai ran to 1:30 a.m., and Kauai officials sounded the Niihau siren as a final signal to move indoors.

Forecasters expect 4 to 8 more inches of rain on Kauai, storm surge of 2 to 4 feet and surf of 20 to 30 feet before Lowell weakens to a 70 mph tropical storm late Tuesday and moves away to the northwest. Public schools, county and state offices and courts on Kauai and Oahu are closed Tuesday. No injuries had been reported by late Monday.

briefs.headline: NTSB says all five Miami crash dead were in vehicles the jet struck
briefs.summary: The 767 overran Runway 30 by about 1,300 feet and hit a van carrying seven cleaners and an SUV, Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy said Monday; the pilot survived with minor injuries, and both recorders were recovered.

briefs.headline: Man accused of lunging at Acton at the Canfield Fair faces court
briefs.summary: Patrick Havas, 38, of Canfield, is held on two assault counts and disorderly conduct after pushing toward the Ohio governor candidate Sunday; deputies recovered two handguns and brass knuckles. Acton was not hurt.

briefs.headline: New Hampshire picks Senate nominees for Shaheen's open seat
briefs.summary: Rep. Chris Pappas faces Karishma Manzur for the Democrats and Trump-endorsed former Sen. John Sununu faces Scott Brown for the Republicans in Tuesday's primary; polls close between 7 and 8 p.m. by town.

briefs.headline: Diesel hits a record $5.90 a gallon as crude climbs
briefs.summary: AAA put the national average at $5.90 Monday, up about 30 cents in a week and from $3.71 a year ago, France24 reported; regular gasoline averaged $4.15, against $3.20 last year.

briefs.headline: Iran vows a Gulf exclusion zone out to the U.S. blockade line
briefs.summary: Security council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said Iran will declare a restricted zone from the U.S. Navy's blockade line into the Gulf and sanction any vessel entering it; analysts count 10 to 13 ships a day through Hormuz, the fewest since May.

briefs.headline: Russian strikes kill two in Kyiv hours after a three-day pause ends
briefs.summary: Mayor Vitali Klitschko said two people died and seven were wounded in Tuesday morning's attack, which hit a five-story apartment block in Solomianskyi; Putin had halted strikes on the capital while U.S. envoys visited Moscow and Kyiv.

briefs.headline: Jakarta's airport reopens as Anak Krakatau ash thins
briefs.summary: Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said Soekarno-Hatta and four other airports reopened Tuesday after closures disrupted about 2,900 flights and more than 340,000 travelers; the volcano erupted three more times Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Egyptian court upholds death sentence for TV host in drug case
briefs.summary: A court confirmed death sentences Monday for presenter Sarah Khalifa and 11 others for drug trafficking, Africanews reported, citing state media; nine defendants got life terms, seven were acquitted, and her lawyer plans an appeal.

briefs.headline: Biohazard signs stand at Kanawha Falls as DEP sues sewer district
briefs.summary: The state has sued the Kanawha Falls PSD over untreated sewage reaching the watershed from a line damaged in a 2022 flood, WSAZ reported; the PSC ordered the district Sept. 3 to stop billing affected customers, the Register-Herald reported.

briefs.headline: Judge defers ruling on conflict claim in Pleasants plant bankruptcy
briefs.summary: Judge Karen Owens deferred a ruling on claims that the debtor's law firm has a conflict, kept a Nov. 18 sale hearing and set a December trial on a motion to dismiss the Pleasants Power Station Chapter 11 case as filed in bad faith, WTAP reported.

briefs.headline: Cecil Roberts ties Marmet's Labor Day parade to Blair Mountain
briefs.summary: The former UMWA president told Monday's crowd that his great-uncle Bill Blizzard led the 1921 march and was tried for treason and found not guilty; WCHS put the town's festival at 70 years.

regional.item: 'Stranger Things' actor Joe Chrest, a 1986 Marshall graduate, will be grand marshal of the Sept. 25 homecoming parade.
Ron Cobb, who founded the South Hills Basketball League and backed South Hills and George Washington basketball for 50 years, has died at 79.
Wood County's assessor says a state Auditor's Office lapse left 107 local properties without tax bills and affected other counties too.

away.item: U.S. 7 between Exit 2 in Bennington and Exit 3 in Arlington closes Sept. 19 through Oct. 3 for culvert work, with detours on VT 7A and VT 313, VTrans says.

hotspots.item: A man and a woman died in a multi-ATV crash near Bergoo about 7:30 p.m. Saturday, close to the Randolph County line; the sheriff's office has not released their names.
Topsail Beach commissioners vote Wednesday at 5 p.m. on allowing up to five hens on lots of 8,500 square feet or more.

briefs.headline: RCMP seek camera footage after gunfire in College Heights
briefs.summary: Police say five or six shots were heard on the 7100 block of Barbara Place about 5:30 a.m. Sept. 4 and a white SUV sped off; nobody was hurt, and Cpl. Jennifer Cooper asked residents for dashcam and security video.

briefs.headline: Tour de North riders leave Fort St. John on Friday
briefs.summary: The 850-km Cops for Cancer ride runs Sept. 11-17 from Fort St. John to Williams Lake, with a block party at the Prince George RCMP detachment on Victoria Street from 4:30 to 6:30 p.m. Sept. 15 to raise money for Camp Goodtimes.

briefs.headline: Tyee investigation asks why 138 B.C. workers died on the job in 2025
briefs.summary: The Tyee, in a piece carried by CHEK, counts 138 workplace deaths in B.C. last year and about 1,000 a year across Canada, and finds that criminal negligence charges against employers remain rare.

briefs.headline: Seniors advocate warns retirees are one rent hike from the street
briefs.summary: The Tyee reports a 78-year-old woman was discharged from Royal Columbian Hospital to a Downtown Eastside shelter; advocate Dan Levitt says 6,000 seniors are waiting for long-term care, with the average wait now 10 months.

briefs.headline: Canada's countertariffs on $28-billion of U.S. goods take effect
briefs.summary: Tariffs of 25 or 50 per cent, and 15 on some items, on nearly 900 U.S. products took effect at 12:01 a.m. Tuesday with talks frozen; pollster Nik Nanos told the Globe that resolve may fade if layoffs follow.

briefs.headline: Trump vows to bar Bombardier jets from the U.S. market
briefs.summary: Trump posted "NO MORE SELLING BOMBARDIER IN THE UNITED STATES" on Monday; the company says it employs 3,500 Americans and that the U.S. supplied more than half of its US$9.55-billion revenue in 2025.

briefs.headline: Melting Svalbard glaciers flush ancient methane from bedrock
briefs.summary: A Tromso-based iC3 team found methane up to 425 times atmospheric equilibrium in all 148 samples from 19 glacier-fed rivers, 182 to 368 tonnes a year from organic-rich shale, in Nature Communications; the authors call it small next to human emissions.

briefs.headline: Acorn worm rewires half its cells during metamorphosis
briefs.summary: A Stanford team profiled more than 87,000 cells of Schizocardium californicum across five stages and found over half changed identity, with larval neurons taking new adult roles, in Nature Communications.

briefs.headline: Permafrost thaw amplified a magnitude 6.5 Arctic quake's damage
briefs.summary: A GEOMAR-led study in PNAS reconstructs the March 10, 2025 Jan Mayen quake, which sent a rock avalanche 7 km onto Kjerulf Glacier, and finds no comparable event in 40 years of satellite records.

briefs.headline: Black-hole 'hair' could show up in gravitational-wave ringdown
briefs.summary: A Nagoya University calculation finds hidden matter around a black hole shifts a ringdown's frequency and decay by different amounts, a testable signature, in the Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics; it is theory, not yet observed.

briefs.headline: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra tops Arena's WebDev board by 35 points
briefs.summary: The Max version scores 1797 on Arena.ai's crowd-voted WebDev leaderboard, against 1762 for Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 and 1688 for Claude Opus 5; the posted confidence intervals overlap at the edges.

briefs.headline: Judge lets Minnesota enforce its AI nudification law against xAI
briefs.summary: U.S. District Judge Donovan Frank on Thursday denied xAI's bid for an injunction, letting the state seek fines of up to $500,000 per violation under the law in force since Aug. 1; xAI has appealed to the 8th Circuit.

briefs.headline: Whitehead neural net reads which signals a cell received
briefs.summary: The IRIS model, trained on thousands of human embryonic stem cells, identifies which of six signaling pathways a cell was exposed to, and its predictions for lung cells held up in experiments, the institute reported in Nature Methods.

weather_ear: Sky and temperature at 7:15, from Jim Claudtore.
kicker: The state Supreme Court hears the two jail-death appeals at 10 a.m.; Nicholas-Webster and Summers ran no regional line, and the Bergoo crash runs under Vacation Hotspots.
